newsitem.title: DENMARK: 1,500 Danish trucks continue German border protest.
newsitem.headline: 1,500 Danish trucks continue German border protest.

text.p: Some 1,500 Danish trucks blockaded the Padborg customs area at the Danish-German border on Tuesday in the second day of a protest action against government plans to cut daily allowances, Danish Radio reported.
"Only truck traffic is affected, private cars are being diverted in and out of Denmark via other points," a police spokesman at the Padborg frontier point told Reuters.
He said the trucks were only blocking the customs area at Padborg but was unable to estimate the number of trucks involved although he said the Danish Radio estimate seemed accurate.
The drivers, campaigning for the bigger tax deductible personal allowances other groups receive while working abroad, met on Tuesday morning to discuss escalating their action.
The meeting was called after inconclusive talks between the drivers and Danish tax minister Carsten Koch on Monday.

The protest spread to other parts of Denmark on Monday night, the Danish news agency Ritzau reported, with blockades stopping trucks from boarding ferries from the northern port of Frederikshavn to Sweden and Roedby in the south to Germany.
It said that Copenhagen and Elsinore ports, in east Denmark, had not been affected by blockade action.
The Danish government was scheduled to meet on Wednesday to consider the drivers' demands, Ritzau said.
